task.title: Commit the regenerated offline dependency manifest and its Ed25519 signature
task.objective: Bring the working tree to a clean state on main by committing resources/dependency-manifest.json and resources/dependency-manifest.sig, which were regenerated on 2026-08-30 and already describe the current HEAD (v0.1.24, sourceCommit 8b469800d4ad14ee8276866b79b4db6f73236fb7, sourceTreeDirty false). The files are preserved by committing them, never by reverting them.

preserved_notes: The two resources/dependency-manifest.* files are dirty at grant time and are the SUBJECT of this task, not frozen bystanders — so they are deliberately absent from preserved_paths, whose fingerprints must survive the task unchanged. Committing them is the preservation.
No reset, checkout or clean is authorised against these files. The regenerated content is the only copy of the manifest that matches HEAD.

acceptance.description: The regenerated manifest pair is committed to main and the working tree is clean, with no user work discarded and no reverting of resources/**.
The digest the signature attests to is the digest of the manifest bytes actually committed, so the pair is internally coherent rather than a stale signature over older content.
The committed manifest verifies against the committed Ed25519 signature and the offline bundle still passes integrity validation at HEAD.

evidence.note: Inspected directly. The only manifest changes are manifestGeneratedAt 2026-08-29T20:14:48Z -> 2026-08-30T07:11:09Z, application.version 0.1.22 -> 0.1.24 and application.sourceCommit 8546453... -> 8b46980..., with sourceTreeDirty false. 8b469800d4ad14ee8276866b79b4db6f73236fb7 is exactly HEAD, and 0.1.24 is the version HEAD bumped to, so the regenerated manifest describes the commit it sits on. The signature file changes only manifestSha256 and signatureBase64; algorithm Ed25519 and keyId ed25519:aa5b9dd8... are unchanged, so no key rotation or signing-procedure change is involved. Committed as 1933077 (2 files changed, 5 insertions, 5 deletions) — the regenerated content was preserved by committing it; nothing under resources/ was reverted, reset or cleaned.

evidence.command: node tools/agents/lease-cli.mjs grant (fingerprints recorded in docs/ai/contracts/active-lease.json)
evidence.note: Executed, not asserted. tools/agents/lease.mjs:175 hashes the raw file bytes with createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex") and recorded baseline_dirty_fingerprints["resources/dependency-manifest.json"] = ebdf1f09105d9582c253063523516219e473287562f4fee0897eb488a96ad99d. resources/dependency-manifest.sig records manifestSha256 = ebdf1f09105d9582c253063523516219e473287562f4fee0897eb488a96ad99d. Identical, and both are raw-byte SHA-256, so the digest the signature attests to is the digest of the exact manifest bytes committed in 1933077 — the signature is not stale over older content. This is deliberately a weaker claim than ACC-3: it proves digest/content binding only. It does NOT verify the Ed25519 signature over that digest against the trusted public key, and it does not re-check the offline boundary; both remain the job of offline-strict-validation.

EXECUTED by the release lease holder at HEAD 6ea461c; exit 0, reaching 'Offline bundle validation completed.' / 'Development mode: warnings do not fail validation.' Zero ERROR lines and zero WARNING lines. Substantive positive output: Oracle bridge jar present at 41.9 KB, and semantic native host 17/17 assets checksum-verified (zvec 0.6.0). The bundled-Chromium branch emitted nothing, which per scripts/validate-offline-bundle.ps1:114-118 is the present-and-pinned path (Assert-AwkitPlaywrightPin), since absence would have printed a message. CAVEAT ON THE Ed25519 CHECK, recorded rather than glossed: no run emits a positive 'signature verified' line, so its success is INFERRED, not observed. Three independent supports, in decreasing strength: (1) the digest binding in manifest-digest-binding is a directly executed byte-level match; (2) scripts/validate-offline-bundle.ps1:61-64 invokes the verify step unconditionally, before any -Strict branch, appending straight to $failures without passing through Add-Problem, so non-strict mode cannot downgrade it to a warning, and the success line is only reachable when $failures is empty; (3) DIFFERENTIAL EVIDENCE from the -Strict run, which is stronger than silence alone — that run had a NON-EMPTY failure list and printed its full contents, and a signature failure was not among the lines printed, proving the failure-reporting path was genuinely exercised and would have surfaced one. This is inference from an exercised mechanism, not a direct observation, and is not claimed as such.

EXECUTED by the release lease holder; exit 1 with exactly one failure: 'ERROR: Strict mode requires manifest application.sourceCommit to equal the release Git HEAD (6ea461cc93cc4c1ce55ad72f93af85249f36e363).' Recorded as FAIL, not hidden or relabelled. It is nevertheless demoted to required:false because it was mis-specified for this task, not because it failed. scripts/validate-offline-bundle.ps1:165-172 asserts manifest application.sourceCommit === git rev-parse HEAD, which no ordinary development commit can satisfy: committing the manifest necessarily creates a commit whose SHA differs from the sourceCommit the manifest names. docs/OFFLINE_STANDALONE_PACKAGING.md:44-46 states this outright — sourceCommit 'is intentionally historical between releases and is not expected to equal the current HEAD during normal development' — and docs/ai/CURRENT_STATE.md:5219 calls -Strict 'the release-only gate'. Forcing it green would require regenerating the manifest, which the same policy (line 43-44) forbids for ordinary development commits. The strict gate is satisfied at packaging time instead: 'Every packaging wrapper regenerates and re-signs the pair as production-offline before strict validation' (OFFLINE_STANDALONE_PACKAGING.md:51-53). Consequence to carry forward: this pair is valid and self-consistent but NOT release-current, and -Strict will keep reporting so until a release cut regenerates it.

scope_escapes.subject: new_dependency
scope_escapes.detail: Derived by tools/agents/task-gate.mjs from the changed paths, and recorded rather than argued away. INSPECTED, not assumed: `git diff 8b46980..HEAD -- package-lock.json` is 4 lines, both of them the lockfile's own "version" fields moving 0.1.24 -> 0.1.25; the dependencies block is byte-identical and no package was added, removed or upgraded. The path heuristic cannot see that distinction. Left UNRESOLVED deliberately: declaring new_dependency: true would activate architect review for a change with no dependency-graph content, and declaring it false would be the manager overruling the deriver on its own task. A reviewer decides, not the manager.

scope_escapes.detail: Changed by commit 0bcf56d (version 0.1.24 -> 0.1.25) outside routing.expected_paths. Root cause: a v0.1.25 release cut was performed under a lease that had been granted for a v0.1.24 manifest-sync task and never amended. package.json is inside the release agent's ownsPaths (tools/agents/routing-matrix.mjs:339), so the WRITER was correct; the CONTRACT was stale. completion.blocking_note: Implemented, not complete. All three acceptance criteria are now proven by executed evidence: ACC-1 by inspection plus commit 1933077, ACC-2 by the byte-level digest match, ACC-3 by ordinary validate:offline PASS at HEAD 6ea461c. The completion gate nevertheless stays CLOSED because qa_status and qc_status are both still pending: routing activated qa and qc as reviewers and neither has reviewed. The manager does not self-approve on their behalf. Correction of record: ACC-3 originally cited the -Strict gate. That was a specification error by the manager, caught by EXECUTING the gate rather than by reasoning about it — -Strict is release-only and structurally unsatisfiable by any development commit (see the offline-strict-validation evidence note). Its FAIL is retained in the evidence list rather than deleted, so the record shows the gate ran, what it said, and why it does not apply. Known residual risk carried forward: the committed pair is valid and self-consistent but NOT release-current, and -Strict will keep reporting so until a release cut regenerates and re-signs it. SESSION ADDENDUM 2026-08-31 (resumption after a context-limit interruption; every statement below was observed live, none carried over from the prior session's report): (1) SCOPE DRIFT. A full v0.1.25 release cut was performed under this lease, which was granted for a v0.1.24 manifest-sync task and never amended. Commits 0bcf56d (version bump) and bb2543f (regenerated manifest pair for 0.1.25) both post-date the grant at 8b46980. `git diff --stat 8b46980..HEAD` is 7 files / 176 insertions / 28 deletions and reaches package.json, package-lock.json and tools/roadmap/assignments.json, none of which are in routing.expected_paths. Three scope escapes and two lease violations (build, package-lock.json) are the honest record of that; they are recorded UNRESOLVED and are the reason the gate is shut. (2) PUSH STATE. main is 24 commits ahead of origin/main and 0 behind — counted with `git log --oneline origin/main..main` and `git log --oneline main..origin/main`, because `git rev-list` is absent from the guard's read-only grammar. origin/main is still 1f29595; the prior session's push never happened. No work is at risk: all 24 commits are durable in the local repository, and nothing has been reset, stashed, discarded, force-pushed or rewritten. (3) v0.1.25 ARTIFACT. `dist/SpecterStudio 0.1.25.exe` DOES exist on disk and is the newest file in dist/ by mtime, which contradicts the prior session's report that no portable EXE was produced. It must NOT be treated as an accepted release artifact: dist/release-provenance.json still describes 0.1.22 (source.commit 8546453, artifacts.portable.file 'dist/SpecterStudio 0.1.22.exe'), and `write-artifact-provenance.mjs` is the LAST step of scripts/package-portable.ps1 (line 83), so the pipeline died at or before provenance. Whether the EXE's bytes are complete is INCONCLUSIVE — its size could not be measured, since Read refuses binary files and every shell stat command is outside this actor's grammar. A grep for 0.1.25 across docs/ returns no matches, so no document claims that release exists. (4) CRASH DIAGNOSIS, not a blind retry. scripts/package-portable.ps1:11 requires 1536 MiB of free Windows commit and its own comment measures the 7za stage at ~654 MiB private commit for the ~828 MiB payload. Assert-PackagingCommitHeadroom runs at line 46 and again at line 74 — before electron-builder, but NOT during compression — which is consistent with the reported death mid-compression and means the guard cannot catch it. (5) CORRECT RESUME PATH, for whoever holds the lease next: `npm run package:portable`. It reads package.json's version and never writes it (line 81-82), so it cannot bump to 0.1.26; docs/ai/COMMANDS.md:99-100 says so explicitly — 'To retry an already committed version, run npm run package:portable; release-portable.ps1 and the dashboard action are for the next semantic version.' Version 0.1.25 is already committed at 0bcf56d, so no bump is needed or wanted. (6) WHAT THIS ACTOR COULD NOT DO. The root session canonicalises to "manager" and the lease holder is "release", so `git push origin main`, `npm run build`, `npm run verify:verifier-classification` and `npm run verify:roadmap-dashboard` were each attempted exactly once and each denied by the PreToolUse guard. They are recorded as BLOCKED / NOT RUN. Nothing was fabricated, no gate was bypassed, and no approval was self-granted: qa_status and qc_status stay pending because qa and qc have not reviewed. (7) FOLLOW-UP RECOVERY PUSH. A later recovery session successfully pushed main to origin/main at 7b934b38fcd9c38990e802ea156a5f737ffbac06 and verified divergence 0/0 after `git fetch origin`. That clears the push evidence item only; the unresolved scope escapes, lease violations, qa_status pending and qc_status pending still block completion.
